- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is still trending up, adjust downward by 3–5% to reflect mean reversion.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong downward momentum, reduce forecasted decline rate by 20–30% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If forecasted price is significantly above recent 10-day average (e.g., >15% higher), apply a downward bias of 5–10% to account for volatility decay.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (±0.3), avoid large swings; anchor forecast to 14-day moving average unless sentiment strongly shifts.  
- For forecasts with high variance in early days (e.g., first 5–7 days), apply a smoothing filter to reduce noise and avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment spikes.
